title: Neon Blasters

jam_rules.theme: Precision aim becomes physical neon destruction.

audience: Players who enjoy immediate arcade input, high-energy feedback and short score-chasing runs.
player_fantasy: My hand is the weapon: every movement aims, every press fires now, and a precise shot can turn a crystal into a chain of neon fireworks.
creative_thesis: A cursor-aimed instant laser makes aiming itself the instrument: exact contact produces directional, source-colored fractures, while deliberate spectrum matching chains crystal destruction into readable fireworks.
design_pillars: First-shot immediacy: pointer press hits in the same input frame and beam ends at the real target surface.
Physical neon disintegration: impact, fracture, varied directional pixel debris, afterglow and reward remain causally legible.
Precision over spam: three beam spectra reward matching crystal cores without making mismatches unusable.
Spectacle under control: authored escalation, readable overload warning, strict caps, reduced-flash options and reliable restart.
core_loop: Acquire drifting targets and read their silhouette, health, spectrum and volatile warning.
Aim with the reticle and hold the primary fire input for immediate, cadence-limited laser hits.
Switch spectrum to match crystalline targets; chain kills, split beams and volatile bursts for score and Overdrive.
Collect temporary power cores, select run-only upgrades between escalation beats and manage arena overload.
Survive until overload, inspect run results and restart with a clean run state.

controls.mouse_move: Aim at normalized logical playfield coordinates.
controls.left_mouse_hold: Fire immediately on press, then at configured repeat cadence; release stops at once.
controls.q_or_right_click: Cycle cyan, magenta and amber beam spectra.
controls.escape_or_p: Pause or resume; simulation and effect clocks freeze together.
controls.settings: Toggle reduced flash, reduced effects, high contrast and mute.

success_criteria: Real-browser title, active run, pause, overload, results and restart are usable without console errors.
Pointer coordinates remain correct through CSS scaling and high-DPI backing stores; held-fire clears on release, blur, visibility loss and pointer loss.
Simulation is fixed-step, capped and deterministic for a seed and ordered inputs; rendering and sound cannot mutate outcomes.
Four target families, three spectra, splitter, bounded volatile chain, Chainlight, Overdrive, five power-ups and seeded run upgrades have observable behavior and tests.
Particles/effects and target count are bounded; stress measurements record environment and p50/p95 frame time without unsupported performance claims.
A tested local browser build and source archive include manifests, hashes, rights status and open human review gates.
